honorific: Forms of address and self-reference register sheet (zh→en): render royal and imperial first-person pronouns (孤, 朕, 寡人) as natural English 'I' (or majestic 'we' where fitting), never literally as 'lone' or 'the lone one'. Render courtier self-reference 臣 before a sovereign as 'Your servant' or 'Your subject' (preserving humble court register, never dropping it to bare 'I'), and render sovereign honorifics like 陛下/萬歲 as 'Your Majesty' (never literally 'Ten Thousand Years'). Render noble, official, clerical and humble self-references (本王, 下官, 妾身, 贫僧/貧僧, 弟子, 小人, 草民) naturally by speaker role and register ('I', 'this prince', 'this official', 'this humble woman', etc.), avoiding awkward repetition and capitalizing recurring character self-epithets consistently. Grade forms of address (大人, 殿下, 太公/員外, 公子, 先生, 师父/師父, 长老/長老) by speaker-to-listener rank ('Your Excellency', 'Lord [Surname]', 'my lord', 'Your Highness', 'Master', 'Elder') rather than flattening distinct social ranks. Avoid stiff Chinese calques: drop demonstrative 'That' before a named character (那<Name> -> '<Name>'), never leak parenthetical folk-etymology glosses into narration, and match singular vs. plural to the actual characters present. Preserve classical and historical logic faithfully: keep negation scope across multi-clause imperatives (e.g. 莫…只管… means 'do not … and keep …', not an affirmative command), preserve correlative conditionals (不A，就B = 'if not A, then B'), delayed realizations (良久…才 = 'only after a long while did…'), exact arithmetic/share divisions, approximate numeric ranges (e.g. 三五 = 'three to five', never multiplication), traditional time units (一個時辰 = two hours; 不一日 = 'before many days'), classical chronicle grammar (e.g. '陆守江夏' = 'Lu was guarding Jiangxia', not a given name), agent/object direction (答应替他 = promised to do it for him), and kinship/generational seniority. Resolve classical idioms and allusions (e.g. 醉生梦死, 卧薪尝胆, 八百里 in Xin Qiji's lyric = roasted ox/beef, not a distance) rather than translating their surface words literally, and format embedded poems and lyrics with explicit line breaks (\n).
